chunks: ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who became forgetful behind an Imam after he had begun the salat (prayer), so he said nothing, did not pronounce takbir, did not recite tasbih, and did not recite the tashahhud until he gave the taslim. So he said:

“His salat (prayer) has been valid, and there is nothing upon him if he was forgetful behind the Imam, and there are no two sajdahs of forgetfulness, because the Imam is guarantor for the salat of the one who prays behind him.”

key_terms.إِمَامٍ: the prayer leader in congregational salat
key_terms.سَجْدَتَا السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations prescribed for forgetfulness in prayer
key_terms.سَهَا: became forgetful or made an inadvertent omission during prayer
key_terms.ضَامِنٌ: responsible or bearing liability on behalf of another in this context
key_terms.يَتَشَهَّدْ: to recite the tashahhud in prayer
key_terms.يُسَبِّحْ: to recite tasbih or words of glorification
key_terms.يُكَبِّرْ: to pronounce takbir in the prayer

ai.seo_question: If a person forgets dhikr or tashahhud while praying behind an Imam, is the prayer still valid and are sajdatā al-sahw required?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a ma'mum who forgets required utterances while praying behind an Imam in congregational salat. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that his prayer remains valid and that sajdatā al-sahw are not required, because the Imam bears responsibility for the prayer of those following him.
